title: Comparing with 比: A is more … than B
summary: 比 is the Chinese comparative. Instead of changing the adjective (taller, better), you place 比 between the two things being compared, and the bare adjective stays as it is.
pattern: A + 比 + B + Adjective (+ Amount)  ·  A + 比 + B + 更 / 还 + Adjective

rules.rule: Put **比 + the thing compared with** before a **bare adjective**. The adjective never takes 很, 非常 or 太, and never changes form.

examples.pinyin: Tā bǐ wǒ gāo.
examples.english: He is taller than me.

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān bǐ zuótiān lěng.
examples.english: Today is colder than yesterday.

rules.rule: To say **by how much**, put the amount after the adjective: **一点儿** (a little), **得多 / 多了** (much more), or an exact number.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de gēge bǐ wǒ dà sān suì.
examples.english: My brother is three years older than me.

examples.pinyin: Zhège bǐ nàge guì shí kuài qián.
examples.english: This one is ten yuan dearer than that one.

examples.hanzi: 这里的冬天比北京暖和得多。
examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ de dōngtiān bǐ Běijīng nuǎnhuo de duō.
examples.english: Winters here are much warmer than in Beijing.

rules.rule: To intensify, use **更** or **还** before the adjective ("even more"). They are the only degree words allowed in a 比 sentence besides 稍微 and 多/一点儿 as amount.

examples.pinyin: Dìdi bǐ gēge hái gāo.
examples.english: The younger brother is even taller than the older one.

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān bǐ zuótiān gèng rè.
examples.english: Today is even hotter than yesterday.

rules.rule: With a **verb plus 得**, the comparison goes either before the verb or before the complement. Both are correct.

examples.pinyin: Tā bǐ wǒ pǎo de kuài.
examples.english: He runs faster than me.

examples.pinyin: Tā pǎo de bǐ wǒ kuài.
examples.english: He runs faster than me.

contrasts.text: 比 says "more than". To say "less than", do not negate 比 but use 没有 (我没有他高). 不比 is rare and means "not more than, perhaps equal".
English changes the adjective (taller, more beautiful). Chinese leaves the adjective alone; the grammar sits in 比.

pitfalls: ✗ 他比我很高。 → ✓ 他比我高。 / 他比我高得多。 很 is not allowed in 比 sentences.
✗ 他比我不高。 → ✓ 他没有我高。 Use 没有 for "less than".
✗ 我比他更高得多。 → ✓ 我比他高得多。 Do not mix 更 with an amount.
✗ 他比我高三厘米得多。 → ✓ 他比我高三厘米。 One kind of amount only.
✗ 这个比那个贵太多。 → ✓ 这个比那个贵很多。 Amounts use 很多 or 得多, not 太.

title: Equality: 跟…一样 and 像…一样
summary: To say two things are the same, link them with 跟 (or 和) and add 一样. Put an adjective after 一样 to say in which respect they are equal.
pattern: A + 跟 / 和 + B + (不) 一样 (+ Adjective)  ·  A + 像 + B + 一样 + Adjective / Verb

rules.rule: **A 跟 B 一样** means "A is the same as B". The comparison is symmetric, so 跟 and 和 are interchangeable and the two items can swap places.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu gēn nà jiàn yíyàng.
examples.english: This garment is the same as that one.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de xiǎngfǎ hé nǐ de yíyàng.
examples.english: My idea is the same as yours.

rules.rule: Add a **specific adjective** after 一样 for "as … as". Use 不一样 for "different", or 不一样 + adjective to mean "not of the same ..." (e.g. A 跟 B 不一样高 means they are not of the same height; to say "not as ... as", use 没有 or 不如).

examples.pinyin: Tā gēn wǒ yíyàng gāo.
examples.english: He is as tall as I am.

examples.hanzi: 北京的天气跟上海不一样。
examples.pinyin: Běijīng de tiānqì gēn Shànghǎi bù yíyàng.
examples.english: The weather in Beijing is not the same as in Shanghai.

rules.rule: **像 … 一样** is a simile ("like") and can describe a verb. It is also used for "as … as" when you name a typical example.

examples.hanzi: 她说汉语像中国人一样流利。
examples.pinyin: Tā shuō Hànyǔ xiàng Zhōngguó rén yíyàng liúlì.
examples.english: She speaks Chinese as fluently as a native.

examples.hanzi: 他像他爸爸一样喜欢运动。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiàng tā bàba yíyàng xǐhuan yùndòng.
examples.english: He likes sports just like his father.

rules.rule: When the two parts are complex, keep the structure parallel: compare like with like (the weather of A with the weather of B), as in English.

examples.hanzi: 我们学校的学生跟你们学校的一样多。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xuéxiào de xuéshēng gēn nǐmen xuéxiào de yíyàng duō.
examples.english: Our school has as many students as yours.

examples.hanzi: 这里的冬天和哈尔滨的不一样。
examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ de dōngtiān hé Hā'ěrbīn de bù yíyàng.
examples.english: The winter here is not like the one in Harbin.

contrasts.text: 比 says one is more; 跟…一样 says they are equal. To say "not as … as", use 没有 or 不如 rather than 不一样 + adjective, which sounds weaker.
同样 is mainly used before nouns and in written Chinese (同样的问题, 同样重要). In a comparison with 跟 or 和, use 一样.

pitfalls: ✗ 他一样高跟我。 → ✓ 他跟我一样高。 The comparison phrase 跟 B comes first.
✗ 我的跟你一样想法。 → ✓ 我的想法跟你的一样。 一样 goes at the end of the comparison.
✗ 他跟我一样很高。 → ✓ 他跟我一样高。 Do not add 很 after 一样.
✗ 北京的天气跟上海不同样。 → ✓ 北京的天气跟上海不一样。 Say 一样, not 同样, here.

title: Negative comparison: 没有, 不如, 不比 and 有
titleHanzi: 没有 · 不如 · 不比
summary: Chinese uses 没有 and 不如 for "less than" and a few structures for "as good as". The negation of 比 does not give the opposite meaning, so these separate structures are needed.
pattern: A + 没有 + B (+ 这么 / 那么) + Adjective  ·  A + 不如 + B (+ Adjective)  ·  A + 有 + B (+ 这么 / 那么) + Adjective

rules.rule: **A 没有 B + adjective** says A is less than B: "A isn't as … as B". The adjective is bare, and you may add 这么 / 那么 for "that / so".

examples.pinyin: Wǒ méiyǒu tā gāo.
examples.english: I am not as tall as he is.

examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ méiyǒu Běijīng nàme lěng.
examples.english: It is not as cold here as in Beijing.

rules.rule: **有** gives the positive in questions, with the same shape: "Is A as … as B?"

examples.pinyin: Nǐ yǒu nǐ gēge nàme gāo ma?
examples.english: Are you as tall as your older brother?

examples.pinyin: Zhège háizi yǒu zhuōzi gāo ma?
examples.english: Is this child as tall as the table?

rules.rule: **不如** means "is not as good as" and does not need an adjective. It can also compare actions: 坐车不如走路.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de Hànyǔ bùrú tā de hǎo.
examples.english: My Chinese is not as good as his.

examples.pinyin: Zuò chē bùrú zǒulù jiànkāng.
examples.english: Walking is healthier than going by car.

rules.rule: **不如** also opens a suggestion: "we might as well …". Followed by a verb phrase instead of an adjective, it proposes a better alternative.

examples.hanzi: 天气这么热,不如我们去游泳吧。
examples.pinyin: Tiānqì zhème rè, bùrú wǒmen qù yóuyǒng ba.
examples.english: It is so hot, let's go swimming instead.

examples.hanzi: 你一个人去,不如和我一起去。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yí gè rén qù, bùrú hé wǒ yìqǐ qù.
examples.english: Rather than go on your own, you might as well come with me.

rules.rule: **不比** denies a claim: "is not more … than". It leaves room for equality: 他不比我高 means "he's not taller than I am (about the same, or shorter)".

examples.hanzi: 他不比我高,我们差不多。
examples.pinyin: Tā bùbǐ wǒ gāo, wǒmen chàbùduō.
examples.english: He is no taller than I am, we are about the same.

examples.hanzi: 这件不比那件贵,都是一百块。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn bùbǐ nà jiàn guì, dōu shì yìbǎi kuài.
examples.english: This one is no dearer than that one, both cost a hundred yuan.

contrasts.text: To say "less", never write 不比; use 没有. 我没有他高 means I am shorter; 我不比他高 only denies I am taller.
一样 states equality. 没有 and 不如 both state inferiority, but 不如 can also comment on value in general (坐车不如走路).

pitfalls: ✗ 我比他不高。 → ✓ 我没有他高。 Never place a negative inside 比.
✗ 我没有他很高。 → ✓ 我没有他高。 No 很 in these comparisons.
✗ 他没有我不高。 → ✓ 他没有我高。 Do not negate the adjective after 没有.
✗ 不如他好我。 → ✓ 我不如他好。 The subject goes first.

title: Gradual change: 越来越 and 越…越…
summary: 越来越 says a quality keeps growing as time passes. 越…越… links two changing qualities: the more of one, the more of the other.
pattern: Subject + 越来越 + Adjective / Verb  ·  越 + A, 越 + B  ·  一天比一天 + Adjective

rules.rule: **越来越 + adjective** describes a trend over time: "more and more …". Nothing is compared with a second thing; time itself is the reference.

examples.pinyin: Tiānqì yuè lái yuè lěng le.
examples.english: It is getting colder and colder.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de Hànyǔ yuè lái yuè hǎo le.
examples.english: Your Chinese is getting better and better.

rules.rule: It also works with **mental or feeling verbs** (喜欢, 了解, 怕, 想): "more and more I like / understand".

examples.hanzi: 我越来越喜欢这个城市了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yuè lái yuè xǐhuan zhège chéngshì le.
examples.english: I like this city more and more.

examples.hanzi: 他越来越了解中国文化了。
examples.pinyin: Tā yuè lái yuè liǎojiě Zhōngguó wénhuà le.
examples.english: He understands Chinese culture better and better.

rules.rule: **越 A 越 B** means "the more A, the more B". Both halves have a verb or adjective, and the second half often follows the first with a pause.

examples.pinyin: Zhè běn shū wǒ yuè kàn yuè xǐhuan.
examples.english: The more I read this book, the more I like it.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ yuè zháojí, yuè róngyì chūcuò.
examples.english: The more you hurry, the easier it is to make mistakes.

rules.rule: **一天比一天 / 一年比一年** + adjective gives the same sense with a stronger time frame and can be used with 好, 冷, 忙, 大 and so on.

examples.hanzi: 他的身体一天比一天好。
examples.pinyin: Tā de shēntǐ yì tiān bǐ yì tiān hǎo.
examples.english: His health is improving day by day.

examples.hanzi: 这里的房价一年比一年高。
examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ de fángjià yì nián bǐ yì nián gāo.
examples.english: House prices here rise year after year.

contrasts.text: 更 compares two things (今天比昨天更冷). 越来越 needs only one subject and a time sequence.
越来越 has no second variable. 越…越 correlates two. Do not mix them: ✗ 越来越…越来越.

pitfalls: ✗ 天气越来越很冷。 → ✓ 天气越来越冷。 No 很 after 越来越.
✗ 我越来越喜欢很。 → ✓ 我越来越喜欢这个城市。 喜欢 needs its object.
✗ 他越学越汉语好。 → ✓ 他汉语越学越好。 Adjective stays in its slot.
✗ 天气越来越冷了很。 → ✓ 天气越来越冷了。 Put 了 at the end, not extra degree words.

title: Degree adverbs and approximate equality: 更, 最, 比较, 有点儿, 差不多
titleHanzi: 更 · 最 · 比较 · 有点儿 · 差不多
summary: A handful of adverbs mark where something sits on a scale. 最 is the top, 更 is further than before, 比较 is fairly, 有点儿 is slightly too much, and 差不多 is nearly the same.
pattern: 最 / 更 / 比较 / 稍微 / 有点儿 / 非常 + Adjective  ·  A 跟 B 差不多 (+ Adjective)

rules.rule: **最** marks the highest degree among a group. **更** means "even more" than something already mentioned. Both go directly before the adjective or verb.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā fànguǎn de cài zuì hǎochī.
examples.english: The food in this restaurant tastes best.

examples.pinyin: Zuótiān hěn lěng, jīntiān gèng lěng.
examples.english: It was cold yesterday, today it is even colder.

rules.rule: **比较** means "fairly, relatively" and is neutral. **非常 / 特别** are very strong. **有点儿** is "a bit", usually describing something undesirable.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu bǐjiào piányi.
examples.english: This piece of clothing is fairly cheap.

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān yǒudiǎnr lěng.
examples.english: It is a bit cold today.

rules.rule: **稍微 + adjective + 一点儿** gives a small difference after a comparison; **一点儿** after the adjective suggests "make it a little more …".

examples.pinyin: Qǐng shāowēi shuō màn yìdiǎnr.
examples.english: Please speak a little more slowly.

examples.hanzi: 这个房间比那个大一点儿。
examples.pinyin: Zhège fángjiān bǐ nàge dà yìdiǎnr.
examples.english: This room is a little bigger than that one.

rules.rule: **差不多** says two things are nearly the same, or that something is almost done. It also serves as an adjective: "about the same".

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen liǎng gè rén chàbùduō gāo.
examples.english: The two of us are about the same height.

examples.pinyin: Fàn chàbùduō zuòhǎo le.
examples.english: The meal is almost ready.

contrasts.vs: 有点儿 vs 一点儿
contrasts.text: 有点儿 goes before the adjective and implies a negative feeling (有点儿贵 = a bit too expensive). 一点儿 goes after the adjective and means a small amount (便宜一点儿 = a bit cheaper).
很 often has no strength in basic sentences, it just links subject and adjective. 非常 and 特别 carry real intensity.

pitfalls: ✗ 今天有点儿很冷。 → ✓ 今天有点儿冷。 Do not stack degree adverbs.
✗ 请说慢点儿一点。 → ✓ 请说慢一点儿。 Use one amount word after the adjective.
✗ 这个比那个比较大。 → ✓ 这个比那个大。 Do not use 比较 in a 比 sentence.
✗ 他差不多跟我高。 → ✓ 他跟我差不多高。 差不多 follows the comparison.
